content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the horizon, particularly when true values show mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp price increases (e.g., 79.80 → 80.50) and fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward trends; true values often dip below forecasted levels after a few days.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually converge toward true values — suggesting a need for early correction.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks; often holds high values longer than actual price action.
- Mean reversion is under-estimated — model holds prices near recent highs longer than they actually revert.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when recent history includes strong upward momentum.
- Model under-reacts to low volatility periods — fails to anticipate price stabilization or downward drift.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
